title: AIC General Insurance – Practice Exam 2 (Updated Feb 2025)

questions.question: Insurance is BEST described by which of the following?

options.a: A method of distributing all losses among many people
options.b: A method of spreading the losses of a few among the many contributors
options.c: A method of rewarding the wise policy holders for foresight in purchasing the coverage
options.d: A method of ensuring large, wealthy companies bear the majority of the loss and the Insured only pays the deductible

questions.question: Your insured has a Basic home policy and auto policy insuring Section A, Section B, Section C, Collision and Comprehensive. They drive into their own home. How will their policies respond?

options.a: Damage to the house, Coverage A of the home policy; damage to the auto, Section C Subsection 2 of the auto policy
options.b: Damage to the house, Coverage A of the home policy; damage to the auto Section C Subsection 3 of the auto policy
options.c: Damage to the house, Section A of the auto policy; damage to the auto Section C Subsection 3 of the auto policy
options.d: Damage to the house, Section A of the auto policy; damage to the auto Section C Subsection 2 of the auto policy

questions.question: Our client carries Section A, Section B, Section C, subsections 2 (collision) and 3 (comprehensive) on their SUV. On the snow vehicle, they carry Section A, Section B, Section C, Specified Perils only. While ice fishing, they hear the ice cracking and in an effort to get away, they put the snow vehicle back on the trailer but forget to attach the tie-down straps. The ice cracks as the SUV and trailer pull away, but the snow vehicle slides off the trailer and into the ice. There is no damage to the trailer or to the SUV. How will the policy you sold on the snow vehicle respond?

options.a: Covered under Subsection 2 of Section C - Collision
options.b: Covered under Subsection 3 of Section C - Comprehensive
options.c: Covered under Subsection 4 of Section C – Specified Perils
options.d: No Coverage

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.a: Stock companies are owned by the shareholders.
options.b: Government Insurers have more freedom under the Insurance Act than private companies operating in the same province.
options.c: The main function of mutual insurance companies is to make money
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: All of the following, except one, have a bona fide “insurable interest” in the property insured. Choose the exception.

options.a: The contract purchaser
options.b: An individual expecting to be a creditor or any property holder
options.c: The title holder
options.d: The mortgagee

questions.question: An agent issued a fire policy on the Insured’s house but collected only half the premium with the balance promised 30 days later. The Insured’s house was destroyed 90 days later and the agent had still not received the other half of the premium. Which of the following is TRUE?

options.a: The policy was void and the Insured received only part of the premium he had paid
options.b: The Insured was paid as much of the insurance limit in proportion to the premium he had paid
options.c: The Insured’s claim was paid out up the policy limits stated on the policy
options.d: No claim is recoverable by the Insured under the rules of The Insurance Act

questions.question: Bankruptcy or insolvency of a policy holder affects the Insurer’s liability as described in one of the following:

options.a: Has no bearing upon the insurance contract
options.b: Required that any unearned premium be considered fully earned to termination of the policy term
options.c: Automatically voids the contract
options.d: Requires that the amount of any prepaid premium be refunded

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct in connection with the 80% Co-Insurance Clause?

options.a: It restricts the insurance payable to less than 80% of the actual cash value of the property
options.b: The Insured can collect only 80% of any loss
options.c: If the amount of insurance is less than 80% of the value of the property, payment may be less than the actual loss
options.d: The amount of insurance carried must, by law, be not less than 80% of the value of the property

questions.question: To obtain a Level 3 license in the Province of Alberta, you must:

options.a: Not less than a Grade 12 education and a list of 100 prospects
options.b: At least five years’ experience as a sales agent
options.c: Been licensed with Level 2 license for at least 24 months of the preceding 48 months
options.d: Been licensed with Level 2 license for at least 24 months of the preceding 36 months

questions.question: The Insurance Act specifies that an applicant must:

options.a: Pass a criminal record check
options.b: Have a good business reputation
options.c: Have a reasonable knowledge of the kinds of insurance he/she will be licensed to sell
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: An insurance agent:

options.a: May be a corporation
options.b: May bind and countersign policies
options.c: May be a partnership
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: Which of the following employees of an insurance agency is NOT required to be licensed?

options.a: An office manager who communicates with an Insured about renewals
options.b: An office employee who sells to his friend and relatives only, because of their unique position in his life
options.c: An office clerk assisting in claims reports and compiling of claims information
options.d: An office manager who also solicits new insurance principally on the telephone

questions.question: Which of the following is a situation that is common cause of E & O claims?

options.a: Recommending the incorrect limits of insurance
options.b: Failure to send amendments to the insured
options.c: Failure to place coverage after being instructed to do so
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: Before an Insurer or client can recover from the broker:

options.a: The broker must have E & O insurance
options.b: The broker must have made an error or omission causing loss to either the client or company
options.c: The broker must be a limited company
options.d: Only the manager can be negligent

questions.question: A cover note or binder letter is interim proof of insurance. Which of the following is not found on a cover note?

options.a: Policy number, premium, location insured
options.b: Inception and expiration dates, named insured, mortgagee
options.c: Policy Term, mortgagee, limits of insurance
options.d: Name insured, mortgagee, location insured

questions.question: A broker’s binding power are conveyed though:

options.a: The Insurance Act
options.b: Their License
options.c: Their agency contracts with their individual companies
options.d: The facet of her being entrusted with policy supplies

questions.question: The Subrogation Clause of the Insurance Act:

options.a: Gives the Insurer the right to require the Insured to assign to the Insurer all rights of recovery against any party liable for the loss to the extent that the Insurer has made payment or assumes liability
options.b: Provides that other policies covering the same loss shall contribute in their pro rata proportion
options.c: Permits the Insurer to take salvage if the claim has been paid in full
options.d: Permits the Insured to take salvage if the claim has been paid in full

questions.question: In the absence of the Broker Manager, a licensed employee may do one of the following:

options.a: Complete an application and confirm to the applicant that the risk is covered
options.b: Do all acts normally performed by the broker awaiting supervision and review by Level 2 Broker
options.c: Complete an application only and not submit through the portal
options.d: Answer phones, invoice and submit policy to Underwriting

questions.question: Misrepresentation is a very serious charge in the insurance business, and means:

options.a: Failure to explain the method used in computing the premium rate
options.b: Requiring the Insured to divulge all pertinent facts in the sale of coverage
options.c: Letting the Insured believe he has coverage for hazards which he doesn’t actually have
options.d: Comparing coverage of existing and proposed policies

questions.question: As a condition requirement of a loan of sum of money, a creditor may NOT impose one of the following:

options.a: That the original policies of insurance be remitted to him
options.b: That insurance be obtained to protect the property offered as security
options.c: That the kind and amount of insurance be acceptable to him
options.d: That insurance be placed through a particular agent or a particular company

questions.question: Under Subsection 2, of the Accident Benefits section of the SPF #1, Death Benefits will be paid in the event that both the head of household and spouse are killed:

options.a: To the oldest surviving dependent relative
options.b: To the youngest surviving dependent relative
options.c: Equally to all surviving dependent relatives
options.d: None of the above

questions.question: Under the Deductible Clause applicable to Sections C of S.P.F. #1, some losses are not subject to a deductible. Under any circumstance, under which situation will the insurer not apply a deductible?

options.a: Fire, lightning, theft
options.b: Fire, theft of the entire vehicle, windstorm
options.c: Fire, theft of the entire vehicle, lightning
options.d: Fire, lightning, certain types of explosion

questions.question: Under Section B, Subsection 2 of the SPF #1, the head of the household is:

options.a: The oldest person residing in the house
options.b: The person earning the highest salary at the time of the accident
options.c: The person with the largest income in the year proceeding the date of the accident
options.d: The oldest male member of the household

questions.question: Under the General Provisions, Definitions and Exclusions section of the SPF #1, a newly acquired vehicle is automatically covered by the insurer’s contract, subject to provisions that the insured is already insured with the insurer, and has all vehicles insured there for:

options.a: 30 days from the acquisition date of the newly acquired vehicle
options.b: 15 days from the acquisition date of the newly acquired vehicle
options.c: 14 days from the date on the bill of sale
options.d: 14 days from the delivery date of the newly acquired vehicle

questions.question: Under Statutory Condition 8, Termination, an automobile contract may NOT be cancelled by?

options.a: The broker
options.b: The lien holder
options.c: The third party
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: According to the General Provisions of an S.P.F. No. 1, the policy would NOT apply:

options.a: On a ferry between Vancouver and Seattle
options.b: In Alaska, New York State, and while driving in California
options.c: In Mexico, on a one way ferry trip between Canada and England
options.d: In Yukon Territories, on a one way ferry trip between Vancouver and Hawaii

questions.question: The Additional Agreements in Section C of the S.P.F. #1 waives subrogation under Section C against every person, who with the Insured’s consent has care, custody, or control of the vehicle:

options.a: Except if involved in a race or speed test
options.b: Without restriction
options.c: As long as they are a member of the Insured’s family
options.d: None of the above

questions.question: Under SPF #1, damage to an automobile occurring within 24 hours after a bill of sale transferring ownership of the insured automobile to another person is:

options.a: Covered if damage due to collision
options.b: Not covered for any loss
options.c: Covered for loss by theft
options.d: Covered for loss if All Perils is carried on the insured’s policy

questions.question: The SPF #1 carries a provision to pay for expenses of legal defense, but these payments are:

options.a: Covered in excess of policy limits as a Supplementary Payment
options.b: Optional at extra cost
options.c: Subject to policy limits and use up the limits of Third Party Liability
options.d: Paid only if policy holder wins court case

questions.question: An insured suffers a loss to their property in the amount of $10,000 based on replacement cost of the property. The insured’s actual value of the property on the date of purchase four years ago was $6,000. Depreciation has been agreed at 25%. Coverage carried under the policy is actual cash value. The principle of indemnity is the basis of any insurance contract and therefore the insurer will:

options.a: Place the insured in the same position prior to the loss and pay $6,000
options.b: Place the insured in the same position prior to the loss and pay $10,000
options.c: Place the insured in the same position prior to the loss and pay $7,500
options.d: Place the insured in the same position prior to the loss and pay $5,500

questions.question: Under a Standard Automobile Application form, which of the following statements by an insured could void loss payment under Section C?

options.a: Incorrect particulars regarding previous driving suspensions
options.b: Non-disclosure of additional drivers
options.c: Non-disclosure of license suspensions
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: A temporary motor vehicle liability insurance card is valid for:

options.a: 21 days
options.b: 30 days
options.c: 15 days
options.d: 7 days

questions.question: Johnny rents his basement of his home to his mother, who does in fact pay rent. There is a fire in the household which results in a loss to both Johnny’s property and his mother’s contents. Whose policy will respond?

options.a: Johnny’s policy will respond to both upstairs and rented basement suite as his mother (relative) is the occupant
options.b: Johnny’s policy will respond to his premises only
options.c: Johnny’s mother will require a tenant policy for coverage
options.d: Johnny’s mother’s policy will respond to both

questions.question: Under Alberta’s Highway Traffic Act (also known as Traffic Safety Act) the owner of an automobile is required to carry which of the following coverage?

options.a: Third Party Liability (Section A) only
options.b: Third Party Liability (Section A) and Accident Benefits (Section B)
options.c: Third Party Liability (Section A) and Accident Benefits (Section B) and Sections C
options.d: Third Party Liability (Section A) and Accident Benefits (Section B) plus SEF 44

questions.question: A man buys a vehicle for his wife to drive to work daily. She will be the principal driver. How do you write this policy?

options.a: Write policy in both names and rate it for him as the driver
options.b: Write policy in his name only
options.c: Write policy in her name only
options.d: Write policy in his name and rate it for her as the main driver

questions.question: Under Section A of the standard auto policy, which of the following is NOT an exclusion?

options.a: Liability imposed by any workers compensation law
options.b: Liability arising from contamination of property carried in the automobile
options.c: Liability arising from the expenses incurred during an investigation
options.d: Liability for injury to an employee engaged in operation or repair of the automobile

questions.question: Under Section A of an S.P.F. #1, the insured agrees to do the following:

options.a: Appoint an adjuster for the insured
options.b: Admit liability for any damage done by the insured
options.c: Appoint the insurer as its irrevocable attorney
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: The insured is prohibited from driving or operating an automobile in all of the following circumstances except one. Choose the exception.

options.a: While insured’s license to drive or operate an automobile is suspended
options.b: Unless insured is either authorized by law or qualified to drive
options.c: While under the age of 16 or other age at which a license may be issued to the insured
options.d: For the transporting of clients or customers proposing to do business with the insured

questions.question: An employer may be held legally responsible for damages caused by an employee who uses his own vehicle in commission of the employer’s business. The employer can effect coverage against this eventuality by purchasing:

options.a: An S.P.F. #1 – Owner’s Form
options.b: An S.P.F. #2 – Driver’s Policy
options.c: An S.P.F. #6 – Non-owners Automobile Policy
options.d: A Business Use endorsement attached to the employee’s automobile policy

questions.question: The application for automobile insurance forms part of the policy. By law in Alberta, therefore, it is necessary:

options.a: To answer all questions from 1–14 “NO” and submit to the company
options.b: To answer only the questions the insured can remember
options.c: To bring to the company’s attention any answers that, because of personal knowledge, you may feel the insured is not answering correctly
options.d: None of the above

questions.question: Ordinarily, negligence must be established before payment will be made under:

options.a: Bodily Injury Liability
options.b: Medical Payments
options.c: Immediate Medical Aid
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true with respect to a Tenant’s Comprehensive Package Policy?

options.a: Would cover damage tenant did to premises if tenant was not negligent
options.b: Would cover damage caused by fire if tenant was negligent
options.c: Would cover damage from Insured’s dog gnawing at the door causing significant damage on one event
options.d: Would cover all of the above

questions.question: Penny McFlurry lost her job but is expecting to be re-hired in 2 or 3 months. Meanwhile she’ll use her van to deliver flowers 3 hours a week for a local florist. She asks you what she’ll need to do with her vehicle insurance to make sure she’s covered.

options.a: No action is necessary as her SPF #1 covers business activities
options.b: Modify her existing SPF #1 to provide for occasional business use
options.c: Amend the existing SPF #1 to a commercially rated SPF #1 until the insured informs us the use has changed
options.d: Added a business use endorsement to her existing policy

questions.question: The Optional Loss Settlement Clause which provides replacement cost (new for old without depreciation) on the contents in a Habitational Package Policy form affording coverage on Section I – Coverage A, B, C, D plus Section II – Liability coverages of E, F, G and H:

options.a: Is available provided additional premium is paid for the option
options.b: Is applicable to both building and contents
options.c: Is available only if co-insurance clause is attached to the policy
options.d: Refers only to Coverage C – Personal Property / Contents

questions.question: The Homeowner’s Policy excludes coverage against freezing of plumbing systems during the normal heating season but only if inhabitants were absent for:

options.a: More than 96 hours (More than 4 days)
options.b: 96 hours or more (4 days or more)
options.c: More than 48 hours (More than 2 days)
options.d: 48 hours or more (2 days or more)

questions.question: Under the Extension of Coverage section of the Homeowner’s Comprehensive Policy form, Trees and Shrubs, which of the following is true?

options.a: 10% of Coverage A but limited to $500 per tree, etc., with named perils coverage
options.b: 10% of Coverage A but limited to $250 per tree, etc., with perils coverage
options.c: 5% of Coverage A but limited to $500 per tree, etc., with all perils coverage
options.d: 5% of Coverage A but limited to $500 per tree, etc., with named perils coverage

questions.question: Under a Personal Article Floater, it is NOT permissible to insure the following:

options.a: Plate glass window, siding, doors, sliding glass doors
options.b: Movie camera and camera equipment
options.c: Silverware, furs, bicycles
options.d: Computer software, jewelry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is FALSE with respect to the Personal Effects Floater?

options.a: This is the ideal insurance for tourists and travelers
options.b: This coverage provides coverage on contents temporarily removed worldwide
options.c: This policy covers artificial teeth or limbs
options.d: This policy does not cover money while the Insured is travelling

questions.question: Stamp and coin collections are best insured by?

options.a: Homeowners package policy (Comprehensive Form)
options.b: Fine Arts Floater
options.c: Personal Articles Floater
options.d: Homeowners package policy (Basic Form)

questions.question: Under Coverage E – Comprehensive Personal Liability (CPL) portion of property policy, the Insurer’s liability is limited to:

options.a: The limit stated in the declarations plus any interest and costs
options.b: The limit stated in the declaration plus any interest charges imposed
options.c: The limit stated in the declaration
options.d: The limit stated in the declaration plus inflation increase

questions.question: Statutory conditions are found in all policies covering the peril of fire and:

options.a: Impose obligations on both the insured and the insurer
options.b: Impose obligations only on the Insured
options.c: Are only applicable in Canadian insurance policies
options.d: Cover property of a third party negligently damaged by the Insured

questions.question: The following would be considered business property and therefore excluded under the Habitational Package policy:

options.a: Occasional rental of Insured’s residence
options.b: Rental space of insured’s residence for incidental school occupancy
options.c: Rental of 4 car spaces
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: Which of the following would be covered under the extension of coverage for Freezer Foods?

options.a: Expenses incurred to store freezer foods in cold storage unit while freezer is being repaired
options.b: Food spoilage when the insured’s child pulls power cord from the wall, unobserved
options.c: Food spoilage when the breaker is tripped, disrupting the power supply
options.d: Damage to the freezer due to insured food spoilage, up to the limit of insurance on Coverage C

questions.question: If a 6-year old deliberately threw a rock through the neighbour’s window:

options.a: The policy would pay all or part of the loss under Voluntary Property Damage
options.b: If no policy was in force, the parents would have to pay for the window
options.c: Would not pay for the window as the child is too young to understand the consequences of his actions
options.d: There is no coverage under the contract

questions.question: Fido bit the mailman who suffered grievous injury. The Insured’s:

options.a: Would not be found negligent if this is the first time Fido has shown any vicious nature
options.b: Policy would only pay for any legal expenses if the Insured was found not negligent
options.c: Policy would pay compensatory damages and legal expenses if the mailman chose to sue the Insured
options.d: Would only pay for the mailman’s medical expenses under the Voluntary medical section of CPL

questions.question: Your client, Bill West purchased a farm. You advise Bill that he requires farm insurance which will cover his dwelling and contents in the farm house, plus the rest of his farm. You recommend an endorsement be added to cover his farm machinery and equipment. This endorsement provides:

options.a: Coverage for scheduled equipment only
options.b: Coverage subject to 100% coinsurance
options.c: All Risk coverage
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: Under Coverage E – Liability of our insured’s policy, damage caused by owned watercraft is not included if it is:

options.a: Equipped with an outboard motor in excess of 20 HP
options.b: Equipped with an inboard motor of 25 HP
options.c: 20 feet in length
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: Generally, the insuring agreement in policies of liability insurance contain all of the following conditions of coverage except one. Choose the exception:

options.a: Bodily injury or property damage must have been suffered by a third party
options.b: The amount of any damages awarded will be included separate amount for punitive, exemplary and compensatory damages suffered
options.c: The amount of any damages awarded are restricted to those that are compensatory in nature
options.d: The Insured must have been legally liable for damages

questions.question: Under Coverage E – Liability, Comprehensive Personal Liability, the Insured is covered for claims arising out of:

options.a: Renting his home to others who he demands have tenants insurance
options.b: Employment as a sales representative
options.c: Temporary or part-time pursuits of an Insured persons under age 21
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: Insurable interest exists when:

options.a: Individuals and mortgagees would suffer financially by a loss
options.b: Bailees have been entrusted for safekeeping or repair of items
options.c: A person may be held legally liable for their actions
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: A form that changes the terms of an insurance contract is called:

options.a: Rider
options.b: Floater
options.c: Agreement
options.d: Endorsement

questions.question: Our insured has an auto policy containing an SEF 20 endorsement. Under this endorsement, following theft of the entire vehicle, coverage for alternate means of transportation under the Loss of Use endorsement commences:

options.a: 72 hours
options.b: 72 hours after report to the police or insurer
options.c: The day after the report of the theft to the police or to the insurer
options.d: The SEF 20 does not provide coverage for theft because the policy does

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an exclusion to a travel insurance policy?

options.a: Participation in professional sports
options.b: Pregnancy, miscarriage, or childbirth, within 8 weeks of the expected due date, or in the case of a high-risk pregnancy
options.c: Pregnancy, miscarriage, or childbirth, within 16 weeks of the expected due date, or in the case of a high-risk pregnancy
options.d: Suicide, or any attempt thereat

questions.question: Bailee’s for hire have a potential for loss to a customer's property while it is in their possession. The extent of their liability may be a matter of:

options.a: Tort law; Contract law
options.b: Common law; Substantive law
options.c: Civil law; Criminal law
options.d: Common law

questions.question: This means an accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general harmful conditions.

options.a: Occurrence
options.b: Accident
options.c: Obsolescence
options.d: Collision

questions.question: Liability insurers place a number of obligations on insured’s in the event of an occurrence, claim or action. Insured’s must:

options.a: Not, except at their own cost, voluntarily assume liability or self-settle any losses, assume any liability, or incur any expense other than first aid, without the consent of the insurer
options.b: Provide the insurer with prompt notification of any occurrence that could lead to any claim, immediately provide the insurer with any legal documents received, authorize the insurer to obtain any records
options.c: Assist in the investigation
options.d: All of the above

questions.question: Conditions indicating indifference to moral hazard include:

options.a: Statutory condition, indifference to loss, moral character
options.b: Financial condition, indifference to gain, moral character
options.c: Perils that could cause loss
options.d: Financial condition, indifference to loss, moral character

questions.question: Insured’s causing unintentional damage to the property of others will generally be covered by their liability policy. Third party property damage includes:

options.a: Physical injury to tangible property; all resulting loss of use of that property
options.b: Physical injury to tangible assets, loss of use of those assets
options.c: Physical injury to tangible property, and resultant loss of use of that property
options.d: Intangible property, resulting loss of use of that property

questions.question: A property insured for 600,000 is valued at 800,000. There is a co-insurance amount on the policy of 90%. When a loss occurs of $200,000, how much must the insured contribute toward the claim? Do not take deductible into account.
Under Liability Insurance policies, the types of bodily injury which the insurer agrees to pay on behalf of the insured include:

options.a: Bodily injury, death resulting from bodily injury
options.b: Sickness or disease, death resulting from sickness or disease
options.c: Bodily injury; sickness or disease; death resulting from any of these at any time
options.d: All of above

questions.question: When not named on the insurance policy, partners in a common law relationship will be entitled to coverage only when they are able to prove that:

options.a: They were living with the Named insured in a non-conjugal relationship outside marriage for a period not exceeding three years
options.b: They were not living with the Named Insured in a non-conjugal relation outside marriage for a period of at least two years
options.c: They were not living with the Named Insured for more than three years
options.d: They were living with the Named Insured in a conjugal relationship outside marriage continuously for a period of three years

questions.question: The Alberta Insurance Rating Board GRID rating program in Alberta:

options.a: Was developed to set maximum premiums that insurance companies can charge for basic coverages for any driving record
options.b: Applies traditional underwriting criteria such as age, gender and marital status
options.c: Does not consider the territory where the vehicle is used
options.d: Does not base grid step based on past losses

questions.question: Statutory conditions are the rules of conduct that both the insured and insurer must abide by. Statutory Conditions:

options.a: Cannot be changed in any way via endorsement
options.b: Can only be changed by legal endorsement designed specifically to override that condition
options.c: Are legally binding
options.d: None of the above

questions.question: Which organization of experts will discuss contentious claims if and when the Insurance Bureau of Canada Intercompany Claims Settlement Agreement (also called IBC Fault Chart) cannot specifically define the situation?

options.a: There is no organization for this, it is always determined by IBC Agreement
options.b: Canadian Insurance Claims Managers Association (CICMA)
options.c: Canadian Insurance Condominium Insurance Act
options.d: None of the above

questions.question: Which organization is responsible for elevating the status of independent insurance intermediaries (brokers) by providing professional development and ethical standards?

options.a: Alberta Insurance Council
options.b: Insurance Institute of Canada
options.c: Insurance Brokers Association of Canada
options.d: Canadian Insurance Claims Managers Association

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an activity that the Insurance Bureau of Canada is involved?

options.a: Development of advisory model policy wordings like you saw through this course
options.b: Claims handling including claims arbitration
options.c: Insurance crime-related investigative services
options.d: Advocating industry positions with consumers, government and general public

questions.question: The administration of the Canadian Inter-Company Arbitration Agreement is provided by:

options.a: Alberta Insurance Council
options.b: Canadian Association of Direct Writers
options.c: Canadian Insurance Claims Managers Association
options.d: Insurance Brokers Association of Canada

questions.question: You have been hired as a Risk Manager of a large company like Walmart. You are not too sure where to start. As a risk manager of this organization with several stores and potential for many losses, controlling risk means:

options.a: Measuring the frequency and severity of the exposures accurately
options.b: Developing a plan to address loss prevention and reduction strategies including loss assumption or risk transfer methods
options.c: Identifying exposures is your only role
options.d: Purchasing insurance

questions.question: In your new role with the large retailer, you must monitor current situation and modify the risk management plan continuously. The store is constantly changing inventories which may bring different risks. The clientele may change and have differing requirements and government regulations often change to set higher standards to protect the client. The market trends change and you should be monitoring and modifying the plans. Why is this necessary?

options.a: If it is determined that the change you implemented is not effective, further changes may be required
options.b: New exposures could develop like selling garden tools when these were not previously sold
options.c: Benchmarks used to measure outcomes may be unrealistic and require modification and updates
options.d: All of the above
